name: Horseshoe Arch
teaser: The horseshoe arch, where the arc exceeds a semicircle, developed in Visigothic Spain before Islamic conquest.

name: Keystone
teaser: The keystone is the central voussoir at an arch's apex, completing the structural system and locking the arch into compression.

name: Ogee Arch
teaser: The ogee arch combines concave and convex curves, creating an S-shaped profile that rises to a point.

name: Pointed Arch
teaser: The pointed arch, fundamental to Gothic architecture, offers structural advantages over round arches.

name: Round Arch
teaser: The round arch, characterized by its semicircular profile, was the fundamental structural element of Roman architecture.

name: Trefoil Arch
teaser: The trefoil arch incorporates three circular arcs (lobes) within an overall pointed or round arch frame.

name: Tudor Arch
teaser: The Tudor arch, technically a four-centered arch, features a wide, flattened profile with a gentle point at the crown.

name: Voussoir
teaser: Voussoirs are the wedge-shaped units composing an arch, each transferring loads to its neighbors through compression.

name: Ceiling Rose
teaser: Ceiling roses are ornamental medallions positioned at ceiling centers, historically serving both aesthetic and practical functions.

name: Coffered Ceiling
teaser: The coffered ceiling divides a surface into a grid of sunken panels through intersecting beams or ribs.

name: Coved Ceiling
teaser: Coved ceilings employ a concave curved surface to transition from vertical wall to horizontal ceiling plane, creating visual continuity and spatial flow.

name: Dropped Ceiling
teaser: Dropped ceiling systems employ suspended metal grid frameworks supporting modular panels, creating a secondary ceiling plane below structural slabs or roof decks.

name: Exposed Beams
teaser: Exposed ceiling beams serve structural functions while creating significant aesthetic character.

name: Muqarnas Ceiling
teaser: Muqarnas represents one of the most sophisticated ceiling systems in Islamic architecture, featuring three-dimensional ornamental vaulting formed by tiers of niche-like geometric cells.

name: Reflected Ceiling Plan
teaser: The Reflected Ceiling Plan is an essential architectural drawing convention that documents ceiling-mounted building systems.

name: Tented Ceiling
teaser: Tented ceilings represent Ottoman architectural translation of nomadic tent traditions into permanent palace architecture.

name: Tray Ceiling
teaser: Tray ceiling design employs vertical or geometric transitions to create a raised central ceiling area surrounded by a lower perimeter.

name: Caryatid
teaser: Caryatids are sculpted female figures serving as architectural supports, replacing conventional columns.

name: Composite Column
teaser: The Composite order, invented by Romans in the 1st century CE, combines Ionic volutes with Corinthian acanthus leaves.

name: Corinthian Column
teaser: The Corinthian order, likely invented in Athens in the 5th century BCE, is characterized by its elaborate capital featuring two tiers of acanthus leaves and corner volutes.

name: Doric Column
teaser: The Doric order, originating around the 7th century BCE, represents the oldest and most austere of the Classical orders.

name: Entasis
teaser: Entasis refers to the subtle convex curve applied to column shafts as an optical refinement.

name: Ionic Column
teaser: The Ionic order, originating in 6th century BCE Ionia (western Turkey), is characterized by its volute capital, slender proportions (height 8-9 times diameter), and attic base.

name: Pilaster
teaser: Pilasters are rectangular columns attached to walls, projecting typically one-third to one-half their width.

name: Tuscan Column
teaser: The Tuscan order, described by Vitruvius as derived from Etruscan temples, is the simplest of the five Classical orders.

name: Acanthus
teaser: The acanthus motif represents one of the most enduring and recognizable ornamental elements in Western architectural history.

name: Arabesque
teaser: The arabesque represents a sophisticated ornamental system in Islamic art and architecture, characterized by infinitely repeating patterns of stylized vegetal forms, geometric figures, and sometimes calligraphy, all i…

name: Astwerk / Branches-Work
teaser: Astwerk represents a late medieval decorative tradition where naturalistic vegetal forms become primary architectural ornament rather than subsidiary decoration.

name: Boss
teaser: The boss represents both a functional and decorative element in Gothic vaulted architecture.

name: Cartouche
teaser: The cartouche represents a distinctive ornamental device combining frame and inscription field, characteristic of Baroque and Rococo design.

name: Cornice
teaser: The cornice represents the crowning horizontal element of classical architecture, projecting outward to protect walls from weather while providing visual completion to the facade.

name: Dentil
teaser: Dentils represent a distinctive ornamental feature of classical architecture, consisting of small, tooth-like rectangular blocks arranged in a horizontal band, typically in the cornice's bed molding.

name: Egg-and-Dart
teaser: The egg-and-dart motif represents a canonical ornamental pattern in classical architecture, characterized by alternating convex ovoid forms and pointed dart or anchor shapes carved in relief.

name: Finial
teaser: The finial represents a universal architectural device for marking terminations and transitions, appearing in virtually all building traditions.

name: Gargoyle
teaser: Gargoyles represent the functional-decorative synthesis characteristic of Gothic architecture.

name: Grotesque
teaser: The grotesque represents purely ornamental sculpture featuring bizarre, fantastic, or monstrous imagery without functional purpose.

name: Guilloche
teaser: The guilloche represents a sophisticated ornamental motif featuring interlaced bands that create a continuous pattern of oval or circular voids.

name: Iznik Tiles
teaser: Iznik tiles represent the pinnacle of Ottoman ceramic art, produced in Iznik (northwestern Turkey) primarily during the 16th-17th centuries.

name: Muqarnas
teaser: Muqarnas represents one of the most distinctive architectural innovations of Islamic civilization, consisting of a three-dimensional ornamental vaulting system formed by tiers of niche-like cells.

name: Plateresque Ornament
teaser: Plateresque ornament represents a distinctive Spanish decorative phenomenon where architectural surfaces receive treatment comparable to luxury metalwork.

name: Rosette
teaser: The rosette represents one of the most universal and enduring decorative motifs in architectural history, appearing independently in multiple cultures while also spreading through cultural exchange.

name: Volute
teaser: The volute represents one of the most mathematically sophisticated ornamental forms in classical architecture.

name: Wild Men / Savage Men
teaser: Wild men sculptures represent complex medieval iconography combining folklore, heraldic tradition, and symbolic meaning.

name: Dome
teaser: A dome is a three-dimensional structural element formed by rotating an arch around its central axis.

name: Oculus
teaser: An oculus is a circular opening at a dome's apex, providing natural light and, in ancient examples, ventilation.

name: Onion Dome
teaser: The onion dome is characterized by a profile that extends beyond the drum before tapering to a point.

name: Pendentive
teaser: A pendentive is a spherical triangle transitioning from square supporting arches to a circular dome base.

name: Squinch
teaser: A squinch is an element spanning the interior angle of a square bay to create an octagonal base for a dome.

name: Architrave
teaser: The architrave serves dual functions in classical architecture: as the lowest division of the entablature (resting on columns) and as the decorative molding framing door and window openings.

name: Door Knocker
teaser: Door knocker design combines functional and decorative purposes, consisting of a fixed mounting plate secured to the door and a pivoting striker element (often ring-shaped or hammer-style) that produces sound through…

name: Dutch Door
teaser: The Dutch door employs a horizontal division at approximately mid-height, with each section mounted on independent hinges.

name: Lintel
teaser: The lintel represents one of architecture's most fundamental structural elements, functioning as a beam in pure bending to span openings while supporting superincumbent loads.

name: Paneled Door
teaser: The paneled door represents a sophisticated joinery solution that addresses wood's tendency to warp and split with changes in moisture.

name: Pediment Door
teaser: Pediment door design applies classical temple architecture vocabulary to residential and institutional entrances.

name: Pocket Door
teaser: Pocket door mechanisms consist of an overhead track mounted to a header beam, wheeled hangers supporting the door panel, and a specially framed wall pocket typically requiring 2x6 or 2x4 wall construction with additio…

name: Portal
teaser: The portal represents architectural composition at the scale of entrance, combining structural elements (arches, lintels, columns), decorative sculpture, and iconographic programs into unified designs.

name: Revolving Door
teaser: Revolving door systems feature a central vertical shaft supporting three or four door wings arranged at equal angles (90° or 120°), rotating within a curved enclosure typically 6.5-7 feet in diameter.

name: Transom
teaser: The transom window occupies the space above a door, spanning the full width of the door frame and separated by a horizontal structural member (the transom bar or head).

name: Tympanum
teaser: The tympanum is the recessed face of a pediment or the area enclosed by an arch above a doorway.

name: Balustrade
teaser: A balustrade consists of a handrail or coping supported by regularly spaced balusters-short vertical elements typically featuring turned profiles with swelling and narrowing sections.

name: Heraldic Altarpiece Facade
teaser: The heraldic altarpiece facade represents a distinctive Isabelline Gothic innovation synthesizing religious architectural forms with political ideology.

name: Isabelline Facade
teaser: The Isabelline facade represents a distinctive late Gothic Spanish style emerging during the reign of the Catholic Monarchs (Isabel and Ferdinand, 1474-1516).

name: Juliet Balcony
teaser: Juliet balconies are architectural features consisting of railings or balustrades placed directly at the threshold of French doors or floor-to-ceiling windows, without a significant projecting platform.

name: Loggia
teaser: Loggias are covered arcaded or colonnaded galleries integral to building facades, creating semi-outdoor spaces that mediate between interior and exterior environments.

name: Pediment
teaser: The pediment evolved from the functional gable ends of Greek temples into a highly symbolic architectural element.

name: Porte-Cochère
teaser: Porte-cochères are architectural elements providing covered vehicle entrances, typically consisting of a passage through or portico extending from a building's ground floor, allowing carriages or automobiles to drive…

name: Portico
teaser: The portico represents a fundamental element of Classical architecture, deriving from Greek temple design.

name: Propylaea
teaser: Propylaea are monumental gateway structures that architecturally articulate entrances to sacred, palatial, or civic complexes.

name: Quoins
teaser: Quoins are decorative and structural elements emphasizing building corners through contrasting material, texture, or projection.

name: Rock-Cut Facade
teaser: Rock-cut facades represent a unique architectural phenomenon where builders create subtractive simulations of additive construction.

name: Rustication
teaser: Rustication is a masonry technique emphasizing the joints between stone blocks through deep V-cuts or chamfers, often combined with projecting or textured block faces.

name: String Course
teaser: String courses are horizontal projecting bands of masonry or molding that encircle buildings at regular intervals, typically marking floor divisions or creating visual proportions.

name: Tympanum
teaser: Tympana are decorative semi-circular or triangular fields that occupy the space within pediments or above arched doorways, traditionally filled with sculptural or painted decoration.

name: Accessibility Ramp
teaser: Accessibility ramps provide barrier-free vertical circulation complying with regulations like the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).

name: Baluster
teaser: The baluster is a shaped vertical member supporting a handrail in a balustrade system.

name: Cantilevered Stair
teaser: Cantilevered stair construction involves embedding steel reinforcement or structural brackets deep into a supporting wall or central spine.

name: Flagstone
teaser: Flagstone paving utilizes naturally stratified sedimentary rocks that split along bedding planes to create flat surfaces.

name: Grand Staircase
teaser: The grand staircase serves ceremonial and representational functions beyond mere circulation.

name: Handrail
teaser: The handrail serves both functional safety requirements and aesthetic expression.

name: Helical Ramp
teaser: Helical ramps follow a three-dimensional curve around a central void or solid core, rising continuously at a constant or variable slope.

name: Landing
teaser: Stair landings serve multiple functions: safety (limiting continuous fall distance), ergonomics (rest opportunities during long climbs), and spatial planning (changing stair direction within building constraints).

name: Mosaic Floor
teaser: Floor mosaics employ tesserae-small cubes of stone, glass, or ceramic-set into a mortar bed to create decorative surfaces.

name: Newel Post
teaser: The newel post provides principal structural support for the stair balustrade, anchoring the handrail at starting points, landings, and terminations.

name: Opus Sectile
teaser: Opus sectile flooring consists of precisely cut and shaped pieces of colored marble, porphyry, serpentine, and other decorative stones fitted together to form geometric patterns or pictorial scenes.

name: Parquet
teaser: Parquet consists of wood pieces cut into geometric shapes and assembled into decorative patterns.

name: Perron
teaser: The perron is an architectural element consisting of an exterior staircase with landings, typically constructed of stone, providing ceremonial access to a building's piano nobile or main floor.

name: Riser
teaser: Stair risers provide the vertical component of stair geometry and can serve structural, safety, and aesthetic functions.

name: Spiral Staircase
teaser: Spiral staircases follow a helical path around a central axis, which may be a solid newel column or an open void.

name: Stringer
teaser: A stringer is the primary structural member of a staircase, typically an inclined beam supporting the treads and risers.

name: Tatami
teaser: Tatami are modular floor coverings constructed with a rice straw core, rush grass (igusa) surface, and fabric edging (heri).

name: Terrazzo
teaser: Terrazzo flooring consists of marble, granite, quartz, or glass chips set in a cementitious or resinous matrix, ground flat, and polished to a smooth finish.

name: Tread
teaser: Stair treads are the primary load-bearing components where users place their feet during ascent and descent.

name: Waffle Slab
teaser: Waffle slab construction uses a grid of intersecting concrete ribs (joists) typically 3-6 feet apart, with solid concrete areas at column locations.

name: Battlement
teaser: The battlement is a parapet consisting of a series of merlons (solid upright sections) alternating with crenels (open gaps), providing defensive positions atop walls and towers.

name: Crenel
teaser: The crenel is the gap or opening in a crenellated parapet between adjacent merlons, providing a defensive firing position and observation point.

name: Machicolation
teaser: The machicolation is a defensive architectural element consisting of an overhanging parapet gallery with floor openings, typically located above gateways, along walls, or at tower tops.

name: Merlon
teaser: The merlon is the raised solid portion of a crenellated parapet, forming the protective barrier between crenels (embrasures).

name: Portcullis
teaser: The portcullis is a heavy vertical sliding barrier, typically constructed of oak lattice reinforced with iron bands and terminating in pointed iron spikes.

name: Tower
teaser: The fortification tower serves multiple military functions: elevated observation, flanking fire along curtain walls, and last-resort refuge (the keep or donjon).

name: Allée
teaser: The allée is a linear landscape element using parallel tree rows to define axial paths and organize spatial sequences.

name: Arbor
teaser: The arbor is an arched or tunnel-like garden structure providing support for climbing plants while creating framed passages or seating alcoves.

name: Belvedere
teaser: The belvedere is a viewing structure-either a tower, rooftop pavilion, or elevated platform-positioned to command prospect over landscape or cityscape.

name: Canal
teaser: The garden canal is a formal water element characterized by geometric precision, linear extension, and reflective surface.

name: Cascade
teaser: The cascade is an engineered water feature employing gravity to move water down a series of graduated steps, slopes, or terraces.

name: Folly
teaser: The folly is a genre of ornamental architecture characterized by primacy of visual effect over practical function.

name: Fountain
teaser: The fountain combines engineering, sculpture, and urban design.

name: Garden Wall
teaser: The garden wall serves multiple functions: defining boundaries, providing security, creating microclimates, and offering support for plants.

name: Gazebo
teaser: The gazebo is a pavilion structure combining solid roofing with open or screened sides, typically featuring centralized, symmetrical plans-octagonal being most common.

name: Grotto
teaser: The garden grotto is an artificial cave structure combining rustication, water features, and decorative geological elements.

name: Ha-Ha
teaser: The ha-ha is an engineering solution to the landscape design problem of boundary without visual interruption.

name: Nymphaeum
teaser: The nymphaeum is an architectural water feature combining fountain, sculpture, and grotto elements within a monumental framework.

name: Pergola
teaser: The pergola is an open garden structure consisting of columns or posts supporting a framework of beams and cross-rafters.

name: Terrace
teaser: The terrace is a leveled platform carved from or built upon sloped terrain, creating horizontal surfaces for planting, circulation, or activity.

name: Baseboard
teaser: Baseboard represents the interior application of classical base design principles, protecting walls while creating visual transition from floor to wall plane.

name: Boiserie
teaser: Boiserie represents a comprehensive system of interior architectural woodwork, integrating wall panels, moldings, doors, and sometimes ceilings into coherent decorative compositions.

name: Built-in Bookcase
teaser: Built-in bookcases represent the integration of furniture and architecture, transforming functional storage into spatial design.

name: Chair Rail
teaser: Chair rails represent the interior application of classical base-shaft-capital proportioning systems.

name: Crown Molding
teaser: Crown molding represents the interior application of classical cornice design principles, translating exterior architectural orders to domestic scale.

name: Fireplace
teaser: The fireplace combines functional heating technology with architectural focus and social ritual.

name: Inglenook
teaser: Inglenooks represent an architectural strategy for creating intimate scale within large spaces while maximizing heat retention.

name: Kubbealtı / Domed Chamber
teaser: The Kubbealtı represents Ottoman architectural vocabulary for governmental spaces combining functional requirements with symbolic expression.

name: Mantelpiece
teaser: Mantelpieces combine architectural ornamentation with functional design, framing the fireplace opening while providing display space.

name: Shoji Screen
teaser: Shoji screens represent fundamental principles of Japanese architecture: flexibility, lightness, and refined simplicity.

name: Altar
teaser: The altar functions as the focal point of Christian worship space, representing both table and sacrifice.

name: Ambulatory
teaser: The ambulatory is an aisle encircling the apse of a church, typically at the east end behind the high altar.

name: Apse
teaser: The apse is a semicircular or polygonal projection, usually at the east end of a church, forming the sanctuary or chancel area containing the main altar.

name: Baptistery
teaser: The baptistery represents a significant building type in early Christian and medieval architecture, reflecting the theological importance of baptism as entry into the Christian community.

name: Bell Tower
teaser: Bell towers represent a distinctive architectural element combining functional, acoustic, structural, and symbolic requirements.

name: Gopuram
teaser: The gopuram is a towering gateway structure in South Indian Hindu temple complexes, functioning as both monumental entrance and symbol of the temple's presence in the landscape.

name: Mihrab
teaser: The mihrab is an ornamental niche in the qibla wall (the wall facing Mecca) that marks the direction of prayer in mosques.

name: Minaret
teaser: The minaret is a tower rising from or adjacent to mosques, serving both functional purposes (providing an elevated position for the call to prayer) and symbolic roles (marking mosques in urban landscapes and expressin…

name: Minbar
teaser: The minbar functions as a central liturgical furnishing in congregational mosques (jami'), serving as the platform for delivering the Friday khutbah (sermon).

name: Monolithic Church
teaser: Monolithic churches represent a unique architectural paradigm where buildings are created entirely through excavation rather than construction.

name: Nave
teaser: The nave is the principal longitudinal space of a church, typically rectangular, extending from the main entrance (west end) to the crossing or chancel (east end), and flanked by aisles.

name: Pagoda
teaser: The pagoda is a multi-tiered tower characteristic of East Asian architecture, evolving from Indian Buddhist stupas through Central Asian and Chinese transformations.

name: Qibla Wall
teaser: The qibla wall embodies the fundamental Islamic principle of directional prayer toward the Kaaba in Mecca, architecturally expressing theology through orientation and decoration.

name: Rood Screen
teaser: The rood screen represents a significant liturgical and architectural element in medieval church design, embodying theological concepts through spatial division and artistic elaboration.

name: Shikhara
teaser: The shikhara is the towering superstructure above a Hindu temple's inner sanctum, embodying the temple-as-mountain concept central to Hindu cosmology.

name: Stupa
teaser: The stupa is a monumental Buddhist structure embodying Buddhist cosmology and serving as reliquary, meditation focus, and architectural mandala.

name: Torii Gate
teaser: The torii embodies fundamental Shinto concepts through architectural form, serving as both practical boundary marker and profound religious symbol.

name: Transept
teaser: The transept creates the cruciform plan that became standard in Western Christian architecture, particularly after the early medieval period.

name: Buttress
teaser: The buttress is a structural element consisting of masonry projecting from or built against a wall to give it additional stability and resist lateral thrust.

name: Cupola
teaser: The cupola is a small, domed structure rising above a main roof, typically square, circular, or polygonal in plan, crowned with its own miniature dome or roof.

name: Flying Buttress
teaser: The flying buttress is a structural element consisting of an inclined bar or arch of masonry carried on a half-arch that extends from the upper part of a wall to a pier some distance away.

name: Gable
teaser: The gable represents the triangular wall section formed between the sloping edges of a dual-pitched roof.

name: Hip Roof
teaser: The hip roof is characterized by sloped surfaces on all sides, with two triangular faces (the hipped ends) and two trapezoidal faces meeting at a central ridge.

name: Lantern
teaser: The lantern is an architectural element consisting of a vertical, windowed structure crowning a dome, roof, or ceiling void, serving to admit natural light and ventilation to interior spaces.

name: Mansard Roof
teaser: The mansard roof is a four-sided gambrel-style roof characterized by two distinct slopes on each side-a steep lower slope (often approaching vertical) and a shallower upper slope (sometimes nearly flat).

name: Rafter
teaser: Rafters are inclined framing members that transfer roof loads — dead load (roofing materials), live load (snow, maintenance), and wind — to the building's walls or beams.

name: Ridgepole
teaser: The ridgepole serves as the highest horizontal member in a roof system, running the full length of the building at the apex.

name: Decorative Spandrel
teaser: The decorative spandrel represents a key element in Art Deco facade composition, transforming a structural necessity into an ornamental opportunity.

name: Setback Tower
teaser: The setback tower represents the architectural synthesis of regulatory necessity and aesthetic innovation.

name: Stepped Crown
teaser: The stepped crown represents the culmination of Art Deco skyscraper design, transforming regulatory setback requirements into dramatic architectural statements.

name: Sunburst Pattern
teaser: The sunburst pattern represents Art Deco's optimistic celebration of modernity and technological progress.

name: Art Deco Terrazzo
teaser: Art Deco terrazzo represents the sophisticated application of an ancient flooring technique to modern geometric design.

name: Zigzag Motif
teaser: The zigzag motif represents Art Deco's revolutionary break from classical ornament, replacing flowing curves with bold geometric angularity.

name: Curved Facade
teaser: The curved facade represents Art Nouveau's most dramatic architectural innovation, transforming static walls into dynamic sculptural surfaces.

name: Floral Ironwork
teaser: Floral ironwork exemplifies Art Nouveau's synthesis of industrial materials and organic design, transforming structural iron from simple functional elements into elaborate botanical sculpture.

name: Art Nouveau Metro Entrance
teaser: Guimard's Paris Metro entrances (1900-1913) demonstrate Art Nouveau's application to modern urban infrastructure, synthesizing artistic vision, engineering efficiency, and mass production.

name: Organic Ornament
teaser: Organic ornament represents Art Nouveau's fundamental aesthetic principle: deriving decorative forms from direct observation of nature rather than historical precedent.

name: Art Nouveau Stained Glass
teaser: Art Nouveau stained glass represents both technical innovation and aesthetic transformation in glass art.

name: Whiplash Curve
teaser: The whiplash curve represents Art Nouveau's fundamental break from classical geometric ornament, embodying the movement's philosophy of organic, nature-inspired design.

name: Béton Brut
teaser: Béton brut is raw, unfinished concrete left intentionally exposed as both structure and finish.

name: Bush-Hammered Concrete
teaser: Bush-hammered concrete involves mechanically striking cured concrete with a pneumatic or manual bush hammer, creating a controlled roughened surface by fracturing and removing the cement paste to expose aggregate.

name: Deep Window Recess
teaser: Deep window recesses in Brutalist architecture result from genuinely thick structural walls (often 50-100cm) combined with windows set back from the facade plane.

name: Exposed Service Tower
teaser: Exposed service towers embody Brutalism's principle of "honest" functional expression, separating "served" spaces (living/working areas) from "servant" spaces (circulation and services) into distinct formal elements.

name: Massive Cantilever
teaser: Massive cantilevers in Brutalist architecture are heavy concrete elements extending beyond their vertical support, relying on tensile reinforcement and structural depth to resist bending moments.

name: Sculptural Staircase
teaser: Sculptural staircases represent Brutalism's celebration of concrete as a plastic, formable material capable of creating complex three-dimensional geometries.

name: Diagrid Structure
teaser: The diagrid system consists of diagonal members typically arranged at 60-75 degree angles, forming triangulated modules that provide structural rigidity through geometry rather than requiring extensive internal bracing.

name: Double-Skin Facade
teaser: The double-skin facade system comprises an outer skin (typically single glazing), a ventilated cavity with integrated shading devices, and an inner skin (usually insulated glazing).

name: ETFE Cushion
teaser: ETFE cushion systems consist of aluminum frames supporting pneumatically inflated multilayer foil pillows.

name: Green Wall
teaser: Green wall systems consist of multiple components: structural support frame, waterproofing layer, growing medium (soil, felt, foam, or hydroponic), plants, irrigation/fertigation systems, and drainage.

name: Mass Timber
teaser: Mass timber construction uses engineered wood products including CLT (cross-laminated timber panels, typically 3-7 layers, 60-300mm thick) and glulam beams.

name: Parametric Facade
teaser: Parametric design uses computational algorithms to generate building facades based on multiple variables.

name: Exposed Structure
teaser: Exposed structure embodies the High-Tech principle of structural honesty-making visible the engineering systems that support the building.

name: External Ductwork
teaser: External servicing represents a core High-Tech strategy: separating served spaces from servant spaces by externalizing mechanical systems.

name: Gerberette
teaser: The gerberette system uses cantilevered brackets projecting from columns, supporting beams at points of inflection (where bending moment reverses).

name: Glass Elevator
teaser: Glass elevator systems externalize vertical circulation, serving both functional and symbolic purposes.

name: Space Frame
teaser: Space frame systems achieve exceptional strength-to-weight ratios through three-dimensional triangulation.

name: Tension Cable
teaser: Tension cable structures exploit steel's exceptional tensile strength to create efficient long-span systems.

name: Brise-soleil
teaser: Brise-soleil represent a climate-responsive architectural element developed as Modern architecture spread to tropical and subtropical regions.

name: Curtain Wall (Modern)
teaser: Curtain wall systems represent a fundamental innovation of Modern architecture, separating the building's structural and enclosure functions.

name: Double-Height Space
teaser: Double-height spaces emerged as a key strategy in Modern architecture, enabled by structural frames that freed floor plans from load-bearing wall constraints.

name: Free Plan
teaser: The free plan principle emerged from reinforced concrete and steel frame construction, which transferred structural loads to columns instead of walls.

name: Piloti
teaser: Piloti represent a fundamental principle of Modern architecture, liberating the ground plane from the building's mass.

name: Ramp Circulation
teaser: The architectural ramp represents a Modern reinterpretation of circulation as experiential journey rather than merely functional connection.

name: Ribbon Window
teaser: The ribbon window emerged as a direct consequence of reinforced concrete and steel frame construction, which transferred structural loads to internal columns rather than exterior walls.

name: Roof Garden
teaser: The modernist roof garden emerged from the functional possibilities of reinforced concrete flat roofs, which could support soil and vegetation unlike traditional pitched roofs.

name: Adobe
teaser: Adobe represents one of the world's most enduring vernacular building technologies, developed independently by multiple civilizations in arid regions.

name: Log Cabin
teaser: Log construction represents a sophisticated timber building tradition adapted to forested regions with cold climates.

name: Rammed Earth
teaser: Rammed earth represents an ancient construction technology experiencing contemporary revival due to sustainability advantages.

name: Stilt House
teaser: Stilt house construction represents a widespread vernacular response to environmental challenges including flooding, high groundwater, marshy terrain, dense ground vegetation, pests, and predators.

name: Thatch Roof
teaser: Thatch roofing represents one of humanity's oldest roofing technologies, employing dried vegetation arranged to shed water through steep pitch and overlapping layers.

name: Trullo
teaser: Trulli represent a distinctive Mediterranean vernacular architecture employing sophisticated dry stone corbelling technique.

name: Windcatcher
teaser: Windcatchers represent sophisticated passive environmental control systems evolved over millennia in hot, arid climates.

name: Yurt
teaser: Yurt architecture represents a sophisticated solution to nomadic pastoral requirements - portability, durability, thermal performance, and structural stability across extreme environments.

name: Herringbone Brick Pattern
teaser: The herringbone brick pattern represents a revolutionary construction innovation solving specific structural and practical challenges.

name: Joist
teaser: Joists are repetitive horizontal framing members that transfer floor and ceiling loads to supporting walls or beams.

name: Stone and Chain Hoops
teaser: Stone and chain hoops address fundamental structural challenges in large masonry domes.

name: Triple-Stepped Platform
teaser: Triple-stepped platforms represent an architectural element combining practical engineering with ceremonial significance.

name: Diagonal Bracing
teaser: Diagonal bracing is a fundamental lateral force-resisting system where a single member spans diagonally across a structural bay.

name: X-Bracing
teaser: X-bracing provides bi-directional lateral resistance by employing two diagonal members that intersect at the bay center.

name: Chevron Bracing
teaser: Chevron bracing (inverted V-bracing) provides lateral resistance while maintaining accessibility at the lower part of the frame.

name: Pratt Truss
teaser: The Pratt truss, patented in 1844, arranges diagonal members to experience tension under gravity loads while vertical members experience compression.

name: Spread Footing
teaser: Spread footings are shallow foundations that distribute column loads to the soil over an enlarged area.

name: Dead Load
teaser: Dead loads are permanent gravity loads from the self-weight of structural and non-structural components.

name: Aqueduct
teaser: The aqueduct is a water conveyance system utilizing gravity flow through channels maintained at precise gradients.

name: Arcade
teaser: The arcade is a covered passageway formed by a series of arches supported on columns or piers.

name: Bridge
teaser: Bridge design addresses span requirements, load capacity, and site conditions through various structural systems.

name: City Gate
teaser: The city gate is a controlled passage through fortification walls, combining defensive, administrative, and symbolic functions.

name: Clock Tower
teaser: The clock tower is a vertical structure featuring public-facing clock dials, typically incorporating bell-striking mechanisms and observation platforms.

name: Colonnade
teaser: The colonnade is a rhythmic sequence of columns supporting a continuous entablature, creating modular spaces defined by the intercolumniation (spacing between columns).

name: Excavation Trench
teaser: Excavation trenches represent essential infrastructure for subtractive architecture, serving multiple critical functions simultaneously.

name: Imperial Gate / Bâb-ı Hümâyûn
teaser: The Imperial Gate represents Ottoman architectural vocabulary for monumental entrances combining functional requirements with symbolic expression.

name: Layered Courtyard System
teaser: Layered courtyard systems represent a distinctive palace organization principle contrasting with European monolithic palace designs.

name: Market Hall
teaser: The market hall is an enclosed or semi-enclosed structure providing covered trading space organized around circulation aisles and vendor stalls.

name: Obelisk
teaser: The obelisk is a monolithic or constructed tower with square or rectangular cross-section, tapering sides, and pyramidal apex (pyramidion).

name: Plaza
teaser: The plaza is an intentionally designed public open space, typically bounded by building facades that define its edges.

name: Triumphal Arch
teaser: The triumphal arch is a monumental structure featuring one or more arched openings, typically adorned with sculptural reliefs, inscriptions, and attic stories crowned with quadriga (chariot) sculptures.

name: Barrel Vault
teaser: The barrel vault, or tunnel vault, is a continuous semicircular vault extending along a single axis.

name: Fan Vault
teaser: The fan vault, unique to English Perpendicular Gothic architecture, features ribs radiating equally from supports to create inverted conical (conoid) surfaces.

name: Groin Vault
teaser: The groin vault results from the intersection of two barrel vaults at right angles, creating X-shaped ridges (groins) on the ceiling.

name: Rib Vault
teaser: The rib vault features projecting stone ribs at the groins and potentially ridge ribs, supporting lighter infill panels (webs or severies).

name: Alcove
teaser: Architecturally, alcoves define subsidiary spaces within principal rooms through wall recesses.

name: Coping
teaser: Architectural coping serves critical weatherproofing and aesthetic functions atop walls.

name: Curtain Wall
teaser: The curtain wall system separates the building's structure from its enclosure.

name: Dado
teaser: The dado represents the systematic tripartite division of interior walls, analogous to the base-shaft-capital organization of classical columns.

name: Masonry
teaser: Masonry construction encompasses a range of techniques from rough rubble to precisely cut ashlar.

name: Niche
teaser: The architectural niche is a wall recess designed to contain sculpture, decorative objects, or functional elements.

name: Parapet
teaser: Architectural parapets serve multiple functions: life safety (guardrail for roof access), fire separation (party walls between buildings), equipment screening, and architectural expression.

name: Plinth
teaser: Architecturally, the plinth functions as a transitional element between the ground plane and the vertical structure.

name: Wainscot
teaser: Wainscot design integrates panel construction, proportional relationships, and interior character.

name: Casement Window
teaser: The casement window represents one of the oldest and most enduring window types, characterized by a hinged sash that pivots from the vertical edge to swing open.

name: Clerestory
teaser: The clerestory is an architectural feature consisting of a high section of wall with windows above eye level, typically rising above adjacent rooflines or lower interior spaces.

name: Dormer
teaser: Dormers are vertical window structures projecting from sloping roofs, featuring their own roofs, walls, and windows.

name: Lunette
teaser: The lunette represents a versatile architectural element combining structural, illuminating, and decorative functions across classical and revival periods.

name: Mullion
teaser: Mullions are vertical structural members dividing window openings, distinguished from horizontal transoms and smaller decorative muntins.

name: Oriel Window
teaser: The oriel window is a distinctive architectural feature consisting of a windowed projection extending from an upper story wall, typically supported by corbels, brackets, or cantilevered construction.

name: Palladian Window
teaser: The Palladian window features a tripartite composition: a central arched opening (typically semicircular) flanked by two narrower trabeated (flat-topped) openings, with the divisions marked by columns, pilasters, or p…

name: Rose Window
teaser: The rose window represents the pinnacle of Gothic architectural and artistic achievement, combining engineering prowess with religious symbolism.

name: Sash Window
teaser: The sash window represents a significant development in window technology, becoming the standard operable window type in Anglo-American architecture from the late 17th through the 19th centuries.

name: Window Shutter
teaser: Window shutters represent a functional architectural element addressing climate control, security, and aesthetics across diverse regional traditions.

name: Stained Glass
teaser: Stained glass represents a sophisticated artistic and technical achievement combining glassmaking, metalwork, painting, and design.

name: Tracery
teaser: Tracery represents one of Gothic architecture's most distinctive features-ornamental stone openwork forming patterns in window heads, rose windows, and wall panels.

name: Transom
teaser: Transoms are horizontal structural members in window and door systems, working in coordination with vertical mullions to create window frameworks.
